title: Ethiopian Mild Chicken Stew
community: All of Ethiopia — the gentle counterpart to Doro Wat
author: Mama Tigist
desc: Ethiopian Alicha Doro — the mild, golden-yellow chicken stew without berbere. Chicken slow-simmered in a sauce built on dry-caramelised onions, kibbeh, turmeric, cardamom, and ginger — with whole boiled eggs added at the end. The gentle counterpart to Doro Wat, served alongside on the same mesob platter.
longDesc: Alicha Doro is the Doro Wat for those who prefer no heat — the same technique, the same ceremony, the same reverence, but with turmeric and cardamom rather than berbere producing a golden, aromatic, mild result. Served on every celebration platter alongside Doro Wat, providing balance.
steps: Marinate chicken in lemon and salt for 30 minutes. Rinse.
Dry caramelise onions — 25 minutes, no oil.
Add turmeric, ground ginger, cardamom, and coriander. Toast in kibbeh 1 minute.
Add garlic and fresh ginger. Cook 2 minutes.
Add chicken. Coat in the golden sauce.
Add pierced eggs. Simmer 20 more minutes.
The sauce should be golden and thick.
chefTips: No berbere at all — this is genuinely mild.
The cardamom and coriander create the alicha aromatic signature.
Same dry-caramelise technique as Doro Wat — the foundation never changes.
commonMistakes: Adding berbere — destroys the alicha character.
cookingScience: See ETH027 for alicha science. In Alicha Doro, the turmeric's curcumin dissolves into the kibbeh fat, producing the golden colour. Without berbere's competing red carotenoids, the golden-yellow colour dominates the finished stew.
sustainabilityTips: Same whole-chicken approach as Doro Wat.
servedWith: Alongside Doro Wat on the celebration platter
healthBenefits: High protein from chicken and eggs.
Suitable for those who cannot eat chilli.
culturalNote: Alicha Doro demonstrates Ethiopian cooking's most profound quality — every great dish has its mild counterpart. The Doro Wat and Alicha Doro on the same platter ensure that every guest is welcomed, regardless of their tolerance for heat.
